newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nightshifts to lift NedCar '97 output - Volvo.
newsitem.headline: Nightshifts to lift NedCar '97 output - Volvo.

text.p: The introduction of night shifts at the NedCar plant in the Netherlands will lift production of Volvo cars in 1997, but not this year, Volvo said on Wednesday.
NedCar, a joint venture between Volvo Car, Mitsubishi Motors Corp and the Dutch government, on Wednesday requested a night shift licence from the Dutch ministry of social affairs.
Volvo Car spokesman Ulf Thorne said the licence would increase the number of production hours by 25 percent to 5,000 in 1997.
"This is in line with our plan to gradually increase production capacity to 280,000 cars in 1998," Thorne told Reuters. This is up from planned output of 145,000 cars in 1996.
"The purpose of night shifts is to be able to utilise investments and production equipment at NedCar in a better way," he said.
The production pace at the plants in the southern Dutch town of Born, producing the Mitsubishi Carisma and Volvo S40/V40 models, has recently risen to around 400 cars per day.
Thorne said 66,000 units of Volvo new series, the S40/V40, were targetted for production this year.
"Increasing the production pace is planned and is a natural development in the introduction phase of new models," he said.
